facts.text: An astronaut uses about 0.84 kg of oxygen each day. That is why the air supply matters so much.
facts.sourceName: NASA Baseline Values and Assumptions Document (BVAD) 2015

facts.text: Astronauts eat about 1.8 kg of food per day on long missions. Good nutrition keeps them strong.
facts.sourceName: NASA Baseline Values and Assumptions Document (BVAD) 2015

facts.text: On the Moon, astronauts get more radiation than on Earth. The Moon has no thick air to block it.
facts.sourceName: NASA: How Apollo Astronauts Survived the Journey to the Moon

facts.text: NASA limits how much radiation astronauts can get in their careers. Too much radiation harms the body.
Solar flares are sorted by size: A, B, C, M, and X. X-class flares are the biggest and most dangerous.
